decisions.statement: A round is asked for at the port the audit service's page states.
A page stating no port leaves the round unasked and says so.
A round is asked for over the loopback address.
A round carries the commit the caller needs judged.
A connection the service refused is asked again, three times in all.
A round still working is waited on rather than asked for a second time.
A wait that runs out refuses rather than opening a round beside the first.
An audit runs for a quarter of an hour, so a wait that is over means still working.
The runtime puts a wait of five minutes on a request of its own accord.
That wait is turned off here, a round outrunning it.
The wait a round is held to is six hours, stated here rather than by a default.
A service answering nothing is refused by name, saying what puts that service up.
That refusal names the deploy rather than the unit or the daemon behind it.
A refusal the service answered is carried back as it was written.
An answer that names no runs is refused rather than read as a round that ran none.
Nothing here runs a check or writes a verdict.
Nothing here says which checks there are.

definition: a round asked of the audit service over HTTP, and the verdicts that come back
